session.question: How do sustainable technologies, such as clean energy in manufacturing and green and reverse logistics, support Industry 4.0 innovation and SDG-based growth in industrial enterprises, and what did the analysis find about enterprise adoption and environmental management?
session.answer:
Sustainable technologies support Industry 4.0 innovation by linking environmental management with digital transformation in industrial enterprises. In the Slovak study, clean energy in manufacturing, green logistics, reverse logistics, waste separation and recycling, environmental certification, employee environmental training, and CO2 reduction were all statistically associated with Industry 4.0 technologies such as autonomous robots, advanced materials, virtual technologies, simulation, and renewable energy. The article argues that these technologies create conditions for industrial development and future growth when aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). (richnak2022impactandpotential chunk 1)

For green and reverse logistics specifically, the analysis showed that they function as sustainability instruments that improve customer-supplier relations and support environmental management. Their implementation was concentrated in large production enterprises, especially in the automotive sector in western Slovakia, with corporate social responsibility identified as the most important voluntary policy tool. Warehousing and storage were the main operational areas where environmental policy elements were applied. (richnak2021greenandreverse chunk 1)

The enterprise-level adoption findings were strong: more than 82% of surveyed enterprises reported implementing SDGs, and over 70% prioritized environmental aspects in management. The principal barrier to broader implementation was insufficient financial resources. Overall, the evidence indicates that sustainable technologies and environmental management practices are already embedded in many firms and are increasingly connected to Industry 4.0-enabled sustainable development. (richnak2022impactandpotential chunk 1, richnak2021greenandreverse chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-df3658fe: The article argues that sustainable technologies—such as clean energy in manufacturing, green logistics, and reverse logistics—create conditions for industrial development and future growth when combined with Industry 4.0 technologies and innovations in the context of the SDGs. It studied 105 enterprises in Slovakia across sizes, regions, and sectors. Results showed that more than 82% of surveyed enterprises implement SDGs and over 70% prioritize environmental aspects in management. Statistical analysis found significant links between environmental management, sustainability in production and logistics, renewable energy use, waste separation/recycling, environmental certification, employee environmental training, CO2 reduction, and Industry 4.0 technologies such as autonomous robots, advanced materials, virtual technologies, simulation, and renewable energy.
From Patrik Richnák and Helena Fidlerová. Impact and potential of sustainable development goals in dimension of the technological revolution industry 4.0 within the analysis of industrial enterprises. Energies, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/en15103697, doi:10.3390/en15103697.

pqac-d6821b79: The excerpt explains that green and reverse logistics are part of sustainable development in enterprises and were studied in Slovak companies through a questionnaire and statistical analysis. The paper found that large production enterprises, especially in the automotive industry in western Slovakia, were the dominant adopters of green and reverse logistics. Companies mainly used voluntary environmental policy tools, with corporate social responsibility identified as the most important tool. Environmental policy elements were applied mostly in warehousing and storage. The biggest barrier to implementation was lack of financial resources. Green and reverse logistics were said to improve customer-supplier relations and support environmental management despite ongoing environmental problems.
From Patrik Richnák and Klaudia Gubová. Green and reverse logistics in conditions of sustainable development in enterprises in slovakia. Sustainability, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su13020581, doi:10.3390/su13020581.

pqac-b93c63a2: The excerpt describes a study on green innovation technology adoption in manufacturing, grounded in UTAUT and tested with survey data from 516 Pakistani manufacturing respondents using SEM and ANN. It found that performance expectancy, effort expectancy, hedonic motivation, social influence, facilitating conditions, and innovation cost all predict green behavioral intention (GBI). GBI had a strong direct and mediating effect on green innovation adoption (GIA). Organizational size moderated adoption differences among small, medium, and large firms. ANN showed green facilitating conditions as the most important factor. The paper suggests these technologies help organizations achieve sustainable development objectives.
From Mohsin Shahzad, Ying Qu, Saif Ur Rehman, and Abaid Ullah Zafar. Adoption of green innovation technology to accelerate sustainable development among manufacturing industry. Journal of Innovation & Knowledge, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jik.2022.100231, doi:10.1016/j.jik.2022.100231.

pqac-27c7f4a4: The excerpt describes a 2023 study on how Industry 4.0 technologies support sustainability risk management and their financial impact. It notes that technologies such as blockchain, Big Data, IoT, cloud computing, AI, 3D additive manufacturing, and technology platforms are increasingly relevant under climate and SDG pressures, and that COVID-19 accelerated digital transformation. The paper’s survey-based analysis found that, in managers’ opinions, the number of Industry 4.0 technologies implemented in sustainability risk management did not significantly affect aggregate financial performance (including ROA, ROE, OPM, NPM, FLR) or the firm’s ability to manage financial risk. It emphasizes that implementing even one technology is a difficult, time-consuming challenge before synergy effects emerge.
From Jolanta Turek, Barbara Ocicka, Waldemar Rogowski, and Bartłomiej Jefmański. The role of industry 4.0 technologies in driving the financial importance of sustainability risk management. Equilibrium Quarterly Journal of Economics and Economic Policy, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.24136/eq.2023.032, doi:10.24136/eq.2023.032.

pqac-dbcdbb55: The excerpt is a 2024 review on Industry 4.0 and cleaner production in energy-intensive manufacturing. It argues that Industry 4.0 technologies can support cleaner production across the product life cycle, especially in manufacturing and maintenance. The review highlights future priorities such as integrating clean technologies, strengthening industrial data security, and promoting circular economy practices. It also notes that deeper application of I4.0 can drive further cleaner production, but requires coordinated action from enterprise managers, researchers, and governments. However, this excerpt does not specifically mention green and reverse logistics, SDG-based growth mechanisms, enterprise adoption levels, or detailed findings on environmental management.
From Shuaiyin Ma, Wei Ding, Yang Liu, Yingfeng Zhang, Shan Ren, Xianguang Kong, and Jiewu Leng. Industry 4.0 and cleaner production: a comprehensive review of sustainable and intelligent manufacturing for energy-intensive manufacturing industries. Journal of Cleaner Production, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclepro.2024.142879, doi:10.1016/j.jclepro.2024.142879.

contexts.context: The excerpt describes a 2024 Heliyon study on Industry 4.0 technologies in Logistics 4.0 for a sustainable manufacturing supply chain. It says IoT, robotics, cloud computing, and big data improve logistics efficiency and support sustainability goals. The study used the extended theory of planned behavior with SME survey data and PLS-SEM. Findings show that using I4.0 technologies in L4.0 affects subjective norms, which then shape attitudes and perceived behavioral control, leading to word-of-mouth and purchase intention. The paper concludes that adopting these technologies can help shippers and logistics providers improve performance and contribute to sustainability in manufacturing supply chains.

In the Slovak study, clean energy in manufacturing, green logistics, reverse logistics, waste separation and recycling, environmental certification, employee environmental training, and CO2 reduction were all statistically associated with Industry 4.0 technologies such as autonomous robots, advanced materials, virtual technologies, simulation, and renewable energy. Warehousing and storage were the main operational areas where environmental policy elements were applied. (richnak2021greenandreverse chunk 1)

The principal barrier to broader implementation was insufficient financial resources.
